scoring_justification: Mixed: λ and Tc at μ*=0.1 compared to paper gold (result-level), plus structural monotonicity and cross-artifact consistency checks.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold values for λ and Tc at μ*=0.1 for MgB₂ and NbB₂, used in numeric checks.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text and Table 3: λ=0.59 (MgB₂), 0.43 (NbB₂); Fig. 3 text: Tc≈23 K (MgB₂), ≈4 K (NbB₂) at μ*=0.1.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact reported values from the original work; no fabrication needed.

outputs.description: Tc(μ*) curves showing decreasing trend with increasing μ* for each material, and cross-checking Tc at μ*=0.1 against results.json.

Headline average electron-phonon coupling constant λ and superconducting transition temperature at μ*=0.1 for MgB2 and NbB2. Compared to paper-reported values with tolerances; ordering MgB2 λ > NbB2 λ and MgB2 Tc > NbB2 Tc is also checked.

output_contract.notes: The tolerances (hidden) absorb differences from using an open-source DFT code (Quantum ESPRESSO) instead of the original full-potential LMTO. The Tc vs μ* curves are also verified for monotonicity.

steps.description: Compare λ for each material to paper gold with 10% relative tolerance; linear partial credit beyond.
Compare Tc at μ*=0.1 for each material to paper gold with max(20% relative, 5 K) tolerance; linear partial credit beyond.
Verify MgB₂ λ > NbB₂ λ and MgB₂ Tc > NbB₂ Tc.
Verify that Tc decreases monotonically (non-increasing) as μ* increases for each material.
Cross-check that Tc at μ*=0.1 in the CSV matches the corresponding value in results.json within the same Tc tolerance.
